issues.title: docs: retire the funder architecture pitch; it asked for a different, larger, older sum
issues.body:
## Decision: RETIRE, not correct

`docs/ARCHITECTURE_FUNDERS.md` was the repository's only funder-facing document, and it
described a **different, larger, older ask** than the one being made this week.

| | This document | The live ask |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | Recurring **annual** funding | **One** all-or-nothing round |
| Amount | $25K / $75K / $150K / **$300K+ per year**, plus a $5K-to-$100K deliverable table | **$14,500 minimum, $48,000 goal** |
| Deadline | none | **2026-09-09** |

The top tier is roughly **20x** the minimum being asked. Pip is driving strangers at this
repo right now; a funder who clicked through to this page read the wrong number.

**Why retire rather than correct.** Reconciling the tiers with the campaign means deleting
the tiers -- there is no version of a four-tier annual ladder that is also a single
all-or-nothing round. What survived that deletion would still be a *second funder-facing
ask* standing beside Manifund, which is the current state and the actual problem. So this
does not split the difference: the rival framework goes, and one ask remains.

## What it claimed, and what is true

Every row checked against the repository on 2026-08-23, not against the document.

| Claim | Reality | Check |
|---|---|---|
| "Windows, Linux, macOS, **Web**" (x3) | **No web export preset exists.** Exactly three: Windows Desktop, Linux/X11, macOS. No workflow performs a Godot export at all. | `grep -E '^(name\|platform)=' godot/export_presets.cfg`; `grep -niE 'web\|html5\|wasm'` on the same file returns nothing; `grep -rniE '\-\-export' .github/workflows/` returns nothing |
| "**Web export**: instant browser play" + "Web export = zero-friction onboarding" | Two of the document's load-bearing *arguments* rest on the build target that does not exist. | as above |
| "$50K / 3 months / **Mobile port**" | No iOS or Android preset either. | `godot/export_presets.cfg` |
| "**v0.11.0**" | `version.txt` = **0.14.3**; newest tag **v0.14.2** | `cat version.txt`; `git tag --sort=-v:refname \| head -1` |
| "**~6,000 lines** GDScript" | **76,949** across 301 files, excl. addons -- **~12.8x** understated | `find godot -name '*.gd' -not -path '*/addons/*' -exec cat {} + \| wc -l` |
| "**30+ tests**" | **1,644** `test_` functions across 166 files | `grep -rhoE '^\s*func test_' <test files> \| wc -l` |
| "**12 workflows**" | **15** | `ls .github/workflows/*.yml \| wc -l` |
| "Builds generated for **all platforms**" (automated) | No workflow runs a Godot export; CI does not build these presets. | `grep -rniE '\-\-export' .github/workflows/` |
| macOS as a shipping platform | **Ad-hoc at best, not notarised**: `codesign/codesign=1`, `codesign/identity=""`, `codesign/apple_team_id=""`, `notarization/notarization=0`. Gatekeeper refuses these without a right-click override. | `grep -nE 'codesign/\|notarization/' godot/export_presets.cfg` |
| "**Open-source**" | Interim **source-available** licence. `docs/copy/budget.json` -> `constraints[1]` forbids the phrase. | budget.json |
| "Production-Ready" x2, "**The architecture is ready**" | `constraints[4]`: no copy may frame p(Doom)1 as a launch, a 1.0, or finished. | budget.json |
| "momentum" doom model | Already flagged retired at `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:11-12`. | that file |
| Footer "Last updated: **2025-12-13**" | Added **2026-07-16** in `5b3159bb`, never modified since. Its self-report and its history disagree. | `git log --diff-filter=A -- docs/ARCHITECTURE_FUNDERS.md` |

**Where the "Web" claim probably came from.** There is a `web_export/` directory in the
repo. It holds one file, `export_summary.json`, dated 2025-10-30 at `v0.10.1`, reading
`"seeds_exported": 0`, `"total_entries": 0`, `"files": []`. It is a **leaderboard-seed
export, not a browser build of the game**, and it is empty. A plausible route to the false
claim is someone reading the directory name. Offered as a hypothesis, not established.

**Not disputed:** the modularity / extension-point description, the data-driven content
argument, and the deterministic-RNG and signal-based-UI points were not re-verified and are
recorded as **UNKNOWN**, not as false.

## What changed

1. **`git mv` to `docs/archive/2026-08-23-architecture-funders/`** -- the retirement route
   `docs/DOC_LIFECYCLE.md` prescribes ("Never delete; `git mv` preserves" `--follow`). The
   body is **unedited**; a header carries the table above so the claims cannot be quietly
   resurrected. `docs/archive/` is excluded from all pre-commit hooks by design.
2. **The old path becomes a signpost, not a second ask.** Two documents already link to it,
   and the retired footer advertised `pdoom.org/donors/architecture`, so deleting the path
   would 404 a funder rather than redirect one. It now carries the campaign link, points at
   **`docs/copy/budget.json` + `tools/render_budget.py` as the single source of truth for
   money**, restates the binding `constraints` block, and states what the build actually is.
   It names **no raised total, no days remaining, and no backer**.
3. **Repointed `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** -- the banner and open question 3, which had been
   waiting on exactly this call.
4. **Commitment calendar regenerated** -- 156 -> 159 UNPARSED, the three dated lines added here.

## Verification

- `python tools/render_budget.py --check` -> `CHECK OK: 7 line items; min column $14,000,
  goal column $48,000; declared gap $500 reconciles.`
- Full pre-commit suite passes on a complete checkout.

## Notes for Pip

- **Not merged, as instructed.** Opening this PR fires `godot-tests`, `enhanced-cicd-pipeline`,
  `quality-checks` and `self-merge-eligibility` -- all four run on any PR to `main` with no
  path filter, so a docs-only change still triggers a full Godot test run. That is why the
  branch was pushed but the PR was left for you. `self-merge-eligibility` is `contents: read`
  and cannot merge anything.
- **One edit reverted deliberately.** `docs/AGENT_EFFICIENCY_AUDIT.md:147` still advises
  "Leave; maybe add a stale banner" for this document, which undersold it. Updating it is
  blocked by **pre-existing** ASCII debt: the file has 33 non-ASCII lines in `main`, and
  `enforce-standards` fails on `:4` for anyone who touches it. Fixing that is a separable
  cleanup, not this PR's business.
- **`pdoom.org/donors/architecture`** was advertised in the retired footer as a live donor
  route. Whether it still resolves is **UNKNOWN** from here. If it does, it should point at
  the Manifund campaign.

issues.title: design: ADR-0020, machine actor identity -- proposed, not created
issues.body:
**D4.** Built and **not released**, per the constraint: *"actually create things without me, but then don't release them... if that raises interesting questions, give me design gates, ADR decisions and stuff."*

Status is **PROPOSED**. Six gates block creation. Nothing exists.

## The observation

> *"every one of the 130 was filed by me not one by a bot account... we can see what my vs the bot interactions with the repos are, which I think is more honest."*

**The word doing the work is "honest."** This isn't a permissions problem or a throughput problem — it's an *evidence* problem.

## What the record currently claims

Every issue, PR, comment and commit an agent produces is attributed to `PipFoweraker`. `Co-Authored-By` covers **commits only**, is **self-asserted**, and is **unqueryable**.

On 2026-08-23 alone that record absorbed a dozen merges, four issue closures, two cross-repo issues and several thousand lines of documentation, all under one person's name.

That's not a lie anyone told. **It's a lie the tooling tells by default** — and it's the silent-failure shape precisely: the false state is the plausible one, and nothing generates an event when it happens.

## The one place I depart from your phrasing

You said *"the same rights as me"*. The ADR proposes **strictly narrower** rights, and the reason isn't distrust of an agent:

**If the bot can do everything you can, "a human reviewed this" becomes unfalsifiable again** — a merge stamped with your name would prove nothing, because the bot could have made it. The separation is what converts a label into evidence.

Live example: three branch-protection bypasses happened today, agent-driven, under your admin rights. Under this ADR the agent could not have performed them and would have had to ask.

## Six gates. Two matter most

**GATE 1 — Does the bot's output count as reviewed?** This ADR makes the split *visible* without making review *true*. A bot identity could make review-theatre easier to perform, which would be **worse than the current state** — today at least has no ceremony to hide behind. Not resolvable by tooling.

**GATE 3 — The existing 130 can't be backfilled.** GitHub authorship isn't rewritable, so the record acquires a **discontinuity**. An undocumented discontinuity is a silent failure by this estate's own definition.

Gates 4 and 5 are argued rather than settled: may a machine *close* issues, and does one identity covering several concurrent agents reproduce the very indistinguishability this exists to remove?

## On the name

Deliberately not fixed in the ADR — a name chosen inside a design document is harder to give back, and your framing was that it's held until the thing can rename itself.

**Gosh and Golly is better than anything I found or invented**, and I want to flag rather than quietly exploit what it does to the design: a twinned pair *"that should really go together"* lands directly on **Gate 5**, which asks whether this is one actor or two.

There's a genuinely elegant two-actor shape here — one that acts, one that verifies, which would address Gate 1's review-theatre risk by making the checking party a separate identity. **But I don't want a name to decide an architecture.** That's the tail wagging the dog, and Gate 5 should be settled on its merits.

So: **`Gosh` provisionally, with `Golly` explicitly reserved** — not spent. If Gate 5 resolves toward a pair, they're reunited by design. If it resolves toward one, Golly stays unused rather than repurposed.

`Kambu` is ruled out on your own instinct and I'd agree — an ur-cat who is still alive is a poor namesake for something that might be deprecated.

issues.title: rulings: supersede this morning's ladder-debt ruling, which was wrong
issues.body:
I wrote a ruling at 07:00 that **contradicted the documented design of the very tool I named as its mechanism**, and did not notice until the tool disagreed with me four hours later over #1280.

## The superseded version

> *"ladder debt is paid when it is incurred, not deferred to build time"*

Applied literally, that forks the ladder on **every gameplay PR** — which the docstring immediately above it calls out as the failure mode the tool exists to prevent:

> *"forking the ladder on every gameplay PR is wrong -- the cut belongs to the release. So this is a QUERY, not a blocker: deferring stays legal, forgetting does not."*

## The replacement

> ladder debt is **DECLARED** when incurred and **PAID at the release that ships it**; deferring is legal, forgetting is not, and the epoch must never fork on an ordinary gameplay PR

The risk the wrong version was reaching for is real, and the new one handles it: an unpaid bump is only dangerous **if a build ships while it is unpaid**. The danger is bounded by the release, not by elapsed time — which is exactly why `--owed` belongs at cut time. Debt sitting on an unshipped epoch is not debt; it's the next release's contents.

## Two things done deliberately

**The superseded ruling is kept in the tree, not edited away.** The convention says the earlier one is *marked* superseded rather than deleted, and the generator enforced it — my first attempt replaced the text, which changed the content-derived id and produced `supersedes unknown id`. Both now exist and the index records the chain in both directions:

```
pdoom1:2026-08-23:40cd814d   superseded_by: ...fa830705
pdoom1:2026-08-23:fa830705   supersedes:    ...40cd814d
```

**A paragraph below the ruling still argued the superseded position.** A supersession that leaves the old argument standing is worse than none — the file then contradicts itself and a reader believes whichever half they reach first. Rewritten to state the bounded-by-release reasoning.

`--self-test` still passes against real history. Rulings index 39 → 40.

Ladder-Impact: none -- docstring and generated indexes only.

issues.title: print_doc: send -print-settings at all, and stop Chromium undoing the 11pt floor
issues.body:
`tools/print_doc.py` landed `43aad94c` on **2026-07-31**, the day before
`coordination/PRINT_AND_PROCESS_REFERENCE.md` was established (`bc7daf8`,
2026-08-01 09:41:00 +1000). It was last touched 2026-08-20 and was never
conformed. Two defects, both measured, neither of which announces itself.

## 1. `-print-settings` was never passed

`send_to_printer` built `[sumatra, "-silent", "-print-to", printer, pdf]` and
nothing else, so **`paper=A4` and the sides choice never reached the driver**.

- The convention rules `paper=A4` **per job**, because the queue default is
  per-seat and not canonical -- measured `Letter` on the G-seat, `A4` on the
  D-seat. The `@page { size: A4 portrait }` rule in `HOUSE_CSS` sets the PDF's
  page box; it does not choose the tray. So the document said A4 and the paper
  came out Letter.
- Sides is a **correctness** rule, not a preference: simplex for checklists and
  runsheets, because a back face you cannot see while the front is clipped
  *hides half the checklist*. With no setting sent, the queue default
  (`OneSided` at present) applied by luck rather than by intent.

Both failures are silent -- `-silent` has no dialog to fail into.

**Fix:** `print_settings_for()`, mirroring the function of the same name in
`coordination/tools/walkpack/build_walkpack.py` (`43cb364`) minus its page-range
argument, which this tool has no `--reverse` to feed. New `--sides
{duplex,simplex,short}` and `--paper`, defaulting to `duplex` / `A4`.

```
duplex  -> duplexlong,paper=A4
simplex -> simplex,paper=A4
short   -> duplexshort,paper=A4
```

**No heuristic guesses simplex.** Guessing wrong is precisely the failure the
rule exists to prevent, so a clipboard document must say `--sides simplex`. The
two fallback paths (Acrobat `/t`, the shell verb) cannot express either setting
and now say so on stdout instead of quietly taking the queue default.
`-exit-when-done` added to match the canonical snippet in §1.

## 2. The 11pt floor was being undone at render time

`main()` raises the base size to an 11pt floor and calls it not negotiable. It
is enforced on the HTML and then **reversed by Chromium**: a wide table
overflows the content box and Chromium shrinks the *entire page* uniformly to
fit, so H1, mono and body all scale together and the result reads as a
deliberate layout rather than a fault. Margins are specified in mm and do not
shrink with it.

Measured through this tool's own `--pdf-only` path at the 12.5pt default, five
real documents in this repo, read back with `pymupdf`:

| document | before | scale | after | scale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-08-07_CAPTURE.md` | 12.49pt | 1.00 | 12.49pt | 1.00 |
| `docs/game-design/ADR_DQ_AUDIT_2026-08-03.md` | 12.34pt | 0.99 | 12.49pt | 1.00 |
| `docs/game-design/WS3A_DAYLOG_2026-07-27.md` | 11.62pt | 0.93 | 12.49pt | 1.00 |
| `godot/docs/qa/SHUTDOWN_HYGIENE_2026-07-16.md` | **8.33pt** | **0.67** | 12.49pt | 1.00 |
| `docs/TOOLS.md` | **8.37pt** | **0.67** | 12.49pt | 1.00 |

**Two of five printed under the floor the tool declares non-negotiable**, at 67%
of the size asked for. Same signature, same fix and same measurement method as
`build_walkpack.py` `43cb364`: `table-layout: fixed`, plus
`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on cells and on `code, pre`.

### The cost, stated plainly

Pages go up. `TOOLS.md` 11 -> 23, `SHUTDOWN_HYGIENE` 3 -> 7, `WS3A_DAYLOG`
18 -> 30. Those pages were never saved -- they were bought by crushing the type
to 8.3pt. `POSTMORTEM` rises 24 -> 27 *even though it was already at scale 1.00*,
because fixed layout apportions columns evenly and more cells wrap; that one is
a genuine new cost rather than a recovered one. `--base-size` is the honest lever
if fewer pages are wanted.

## Left alone deliberately

- `@page { size: A4 portrait; margin: 14mm 13mm; }` and the 11pt floor. Both
  predate the convention and neither conflicts with it. Alignment, not taste.
- Every other type value in `HOUSE_CSS`.

## Not done -- each is larger than a conformance fix

- **No `PRINTED` stamp and no `PAGE n OF m`.** `build_walkpack.py` implements
  both as PDF post-processing: `stamp_page_numbers` (62 lines) and
  `stamp_printed_time` (65 lines), built on `pypdf` **plus** `reportlab`.
  Neither package appears in this repo's `requirements.txt`,
  `requirements-dev.txt` or `pyproject.toml`. Two new dependencies and ~190
  lines is a design decision, not a defect fix. Flagging rather than
  half-doing it, as asked.
- **The exit code is still treated as evidence.** `send_to_printer` raises
  `SystemExit` on a non-zero return. §1 rules that a print is verified on the
  **spooler**, and records SumatraPDF 3.6.1 returning exit 1 on a job that
  demonstrably printed. So this check can report a false failure on a document
  that is already on paper -- which invites a reprint. It needs the
  `_SpoolerWatch` pattern ported, not a one-line edit.
- **Authored HTML with its own `<style>` still bypasses `HOUSE_CSS`** by design
  (the fragment's style is meant to win), so a full HTML document with a wide
  table keeps the exposure. Only Markdown input and bare body fragments are
  covered by the guard.

## UNKNOWN

- Whether the driver honours `paper=A4` **on this particular queue** is not
  established here, because establishing it means printing. The change makes
  the request; it does not prove the tray obeyed.
- Whether any real document was ever printed on Letter by this tool. There is
  no print ledger in this repo to check against -- unlike `beacon-internal`,
  where the six Letter+simplex sheets are written up.

## Nothing was printed

Every number above comes from `--pdf-only` renders into a scratch directory,
read back with `pymupdf`. No job was sent to any printer, per Pip's instruction
not to reprint anything already on paper.

issues.title: Hiring pipeline: five things the sim knows and the panel never says -- five faces for six candidates, free offer retries, an invisible ad campaign, empty counter-offers, and the onboarding bill you only see after you commit

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Five separate complaints from Pip, filed as one issue
because they are the same defect wearing five hats: **the hiring pipeline models more
state than it shows, and the state it hides is exactly the state a player needs to make
the next decision.** Every fix lands in `godot/scripts/core/hiring_pipeline.gd` and
`godot/scripts/ui/hiring_panel_controller.gd`.

Not a duplicate of `#1219` (the refusal never reaches a visible surface) or `#1218`
(costs not disclosed). Everything below is about **outcomes and history** -- what
happened, what is still happening, and what it will cost later.

---

## 1. The pool of six can only ever show five faces

Pip asked for many more portraits, "a systematic persona run". The measured state makes
that stronger than a wishlist:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Identity slots a researcher can be minted with (`researcher.gd:101`, `IDENTITY_POOL_SIZE`) | **24** |
| Portraits wired into the game (`portrait_library.gd:19-25`, `PORTRAIT_STEMS`) | **5** |
| Distinct portraits already generated and sitting in the repo | **34** |
| Max simultaneous candidates (`game_state.gd:172`, `MAX_CANDIDATES`) | **6** |

`_index_for()` (`portrait_library.gd:62-73`) is a bare `int(NN) % 5` over the 24 slots,
with no roster awareness. **By pigeonhole, a full candidate pool is guaranteed to contain
a duplicate face**, and the four founding candidates collide often. There is no
de-duplication and no placeholder path -- a missing file just renders the card text-only
(`:39-51`).

The art is not the blocker. On disk, unwired:

- `art_generated/researcher_portraits_pilot/v1/` -- 24 distinct portraits (2 style poles x
  6 archetypes x 2 versions), including a sixth archetype `fresh_grad_believer` that was
  never staged.
- `art_generated/round3_rerolls/v1/` -- 10 distinct portraits, prompts hardened against
  anime drift, deliberately varying gender and ethnicity per archetype.

The generation pipeline is also already built and schema'd:
`art_prompts/researcher_portraits_pilot.yaml` and `art_prompts/round3_rerolls.yaml` carry
`schema_version`, style poles, per-asset `prompt_tail` persona text, and a
`generation_history` with model, prompt hash and `cost_usd: 0.06` per image. **A systematic
persona run is a config file and a promotion pass, not a new capability** -- the same
shape as the share/promote route in `#1166`.

Two more facts for whoever picks it up:
- Only the `_256` variant is ever loaded (`portrait_library.gd:14`); the 512 and 1024 PNGs
  are dead weight in the `.pck`. See `#787` for why that matters.
- `godot/assets/portraits/README.md` describes the intended system as *"per-archetype
  variant pools with random assignment"* -- unbuilt -- and still claims the portraits are
  *"STAGED-BUT-UNWIRED. No UI slot references these yet"*, which is stale.
- The floor-sprite pool (`worker_variant_pool.gd`, 5 variants) indexes `appearance_id`
  **independently** of the portrait pool, so a person's card face and their office sprite
  are uncorrelated. Same person, two unrelated appearances.

## 2. A rejected offer leaves no mark, so the same lowball can be sent forever

Pip reported that repeated offers to the same candidate fail silently. The truth is worse
than silent failure: **the second offer is not a failure at all, it is a free retry.**

There is a guard against a *concurrent* second offer and it works cleanly --
`hiring_pipeline.gd:285-286` refuses with `"%s already has an offer out."`, spends nothing,
and the button is disabled with a matching tooltip (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:250-255`).

**There is no guard, and no memory, once the first offer resolves.** Grep for
`already_offered` / `offers_made` / `offer_count` across `godot/**/*.gd`: zero hits.
`Researcher` carries no offer history; the only lifecycle field is `HireState`, and a
rejection returns the candidate to `CANDIDATE_IN_POOL` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:317`)
**unchanged** -- same `self_worth_floor`, same appetites, no resentment, no reputation
cost, no recollection.

`_resolve_offer` (`:304-321`) rejects with probability
`clampf(shortfall_frac * 2.0, 0.0, 1.0)`. So **any offer with `shortfall_frac < 0.5` is a
guaranteed eventual hire** by re-sending the identical lowball every 2 workdays at 1
Attention, until the roll finally lands -- as a `resentful_accept` (-15 loyalty, one
`Ledger.resentment_debt`). The negotiation read, the self-worth floor and the resentment
mechanic are all real; retry defeats all three.

**And the rejection itself is never told to the player.** `_resolve_offer` produces an
`offer_rejected` event at `:318`; grep for `offer_rejected` outside `hiring_pipeline.gd`
returns **zero consumers**. This is the same shape as `#1219` but on the resolution path
rather than the queue path -- fixing `#1219` will not surface it.

Two adjacent holes in the same function:
- `make_offer` checks only `KIND_OFFER`, not `KIND_INTERVIEW`. Offering during an in-flight
  interview is allowed; on accept the candidate leaves the pool (`:329`), the orphaned
  interview job later finds `find_pool_candidate == null` (`:712-713`) and is **silently
  dropped** -- 2 Attention burned, no message.
- The Attention refund on a refused offer is a raw field poke,
  `state.month_plan.attention_spent -= cost_att` (`:292`), not an API call. Worth a look
  alongside the accounting in the Action Queue issue.

**Also worth ruling on:** the offer dialog seeds the SpinBox with `read["mid"]`
(`hiring_panel_controller.gd:497`). With a recruiter `mid == floor` exactly (`:266`);
without one, `mid == salary_expectation >= floor`. Since acceptance is `cash >= floor`
(`:309`), **clicking "Send Offer" without touching the number is a guaranteed clean accept
in both cases.** The negotiation only exists if the player chooses to make it exist.

## 3. Advertise: $8,000 and 3 Attention buy an invisible thing

Pip: *"if a candidate joins the pool, that would be cool."* What actually happens:

`advertise` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:107-127`) costs **$8,000 + 3 Attention**, grants +1
reputation immediately, and adds **nothing to the pool**. It appends a campaign
(`:122-126`) with `campaign_months = 3`, `per_month_min = 0`, `per_month_max = 2`.
Candidates are drawn only at month boundaries (`_tick_campaigns`, `:754-770`;
`month_controller.gd:406-410`), `randi_range(0, 2)` per month.

**Expected yield 0-6 over three months, mean 3, and a 1-in-27 chance of paying $8,000 for
literally nothing.**

What the player is told:

1. Once, on click: `"Launched a hiring ad campaign (candidates trickle in over the coming
   months)."`
2. Monthly, **only on a hit**: `_surface_hiring_notifications` (`month_controller.gd:426-447`)
   emits one feed line per month and **returns early when `ad_hits <= 0`** -- a zero-yield
   month says nothing at all. Which is indistinguishable from the campaign having ended.
3. Nothing else, ever. `update_inflight_display` (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:569-666`)
   renders `hiring.jobs` and onboarding rows and **never reads `hiring.campaigns`.** There
   is no months-remaining indicator anywhere. See the Action Queue issue: this is also the
   3 Attention that appear in the header and in no panel.

The at-cap silent discard is **already filed** -- `#961` records that if the pool is at
`MAX_CANDIDATES = 6`, `_add_sourced_candidate` returns `false` (`:183-189`) and
`_tick_campaigns` (`:763-765`) appends no event, so *"paid campaign candidates are silently
discarded at cap"*. That issue rules that "what happens at cap must NEVER be silent". **The
finding here is the case below the cap**, which `#961` does not cover: a campaign running
normally, under the cap, is invisible from launch to first hit, and a zero-yield month is
indistinguishable from no campaign at all.

And the stale claim already noted in the legibility issue: `action_bar_renderer.gd:68-74`
greys `advertise` out as COMING SOON and its comment asserts this applies "everywhere it
renders (action bar + hiring submenu)". **It does not** -- the hiring panel's own Advertise
button (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:90-96`) is fully enabled with no such warning. One of
those two surfaces is lying, and per `#1221` we now have a convention for saying which.

## 4. Counter-offers: "low specificity" is exactly right

There is **no counter-offer mechanic in the hiring pipeline at all.** Grep for
`counter_offer|counteroffer|negotiat` across `godot/scripts` + `godot/data` returns the
`negotiation_read` docstrings and three hardcoded event options -- nothing else. What the
pipeline has is a **one-shot offer with a read**: two player-controlled parameters (a cash
SpinBox, and four promise checkboxes keyed to appetites at `hiring_pipeline.gd:71-76`),
resolved 2 workdays later as accept / resentful-accept / reject. No candidate response, no
"they want $X more", no second round.

The three things actually labelled counter-offer are all rival-retention events, all fixed
price, all anonymous:

| Event | Option | Cost | Effect | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rival_poaching` | **"Counter-Offer"** | $80,000 | **`effects: {}` -- empty** | `core_events.json:270-278` |
| `researcher_poached` | "Match Their Offer" | $50,000 | `reputation: +2` | `core_events.json:1069-1080` |
| `researcher_poached` | "Counter with Promotion" | $30,000 + 1 Attention | `reputation: +3` | `core_events.json:1081-1092` |

**No person is named** (the event fires against an anonymous "top researcher"), no amount
is chosen, and **no `Researcher.current_salary` is ever changed by any of them.** The
$80,000 option's only mechanical effect is that you did not take the other option. That is
the "low specificity" Pip felt, measured.

The pieces to fix it already exist -- `negotiation_read` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:247-269`)
gives a named band, and the appetite/promise system gives non-cash levers. A retention
counter-offer should be able to use both, against a named person.

## 5. Onboarding obligations: the Attention is previewed, the money is not

Pip wants a checklist of what a hire will require, before committing. Half of it exists,
and the ask is already on record: `#789` item 1 asks that laptop-provisioning and mentoring
*"act as predictable AP sinks you can plan for **when you make the offer**"*. **This section
is the measurement of how far short the shipped dialog falls of that.**

**The full obligation set a single hire creates:**

| Obligation | Attention | Money | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `laptop` | 1 | **$3,000** | `hiring_pipeline.gd:64`, `hiring.onboarding.laptop_money` |
| `visa` -- **only if `needs_visa`, which is `serial % 4 == 0`, i.e. 1 hire in 4** | 2 | **$5,000** | `:97-100`, `:394-395` |
| `systems` (hard-requires `laptop`) | 1 | 0 | `:65`, `:487-488` |
| `meet_people` | 1 | 0 | `:66` |
| mentoring (optional) | 2 | 0 | `:67` |
| **Total** | **3-5 Att** | **$3,000-$8,000** | |
| Until the checklist clears | | | **x0.4 output** (`researcher.gd:303-304`) |
| If mentoring is skipped | | | **x0.85 output forever** + **15% quit roll per month** (`hiring_pipeline.gd:773-788`) |
| Salary | | annual/260 **every turn** | `turn_manager.gd:139`, `clock.gd:38-44` |
| A desk, permanently | | | `office.gd:99-100`; caps 2/4/7/9 by tier, `godot/data/office/offices.json` |
| Each ticked promise | | | a real `Ledger` payable, fuse 8-12 (`ledger.gd:143-148`) |
| A below-floor accept | | | `resentment_debt` (principal 1500, fuse 6) + **-15 loyalty** |

A fully mentored onboard is **5 Attention out of ~20 for the month** -- a quarter of the
month's decision budget, per hire, and that is deliberate (`hiring_pipeline.gd:44-62`).

**What the offer dialog previews** (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:473-484`):

> If they accept: onboarding costs ~%d Attention (+%d optional mentoring). Reserve on hand: %d.

plus per-promise ledger cost text (`:520-521`), e.g. *"owes 1 first-author paper slot in
~10 turns"*. That is good, and it is the model for the rest.

**What it does not preview:**

1. **The onboarding cash.** `hard_checklist_money()` exists (`hiring_pipeline.gd:451-456`)
   and is called from `build_onboard_prompt`, `_provision_hard_checklist`, `_resolve_job`
   and tests -- **never from the offer dialog.** The dialog computes the Attention and
   omits the money on the adjacent line. The number first appears on the
   `"<name> said yes"` card (`:572-607`), where it rides `costs: {"money": money}`
   (`:596-597`) -- **after the player is committed.**
2. **The visa.** `needs_visa` is not in `get_card_data()` (`researcher.gd:707-729`) and not
   on the candidate card. A $5,000 / 2-Attention hire is indistinguishable from a $0 / 0
   one except by reading `~5` instead of `~3`.
3. **Recurring payroll.** The field is captioned `"Cash offer ($/yr):"` with no per-month
   burn and no runway-after-this-hire.
4. **Desk space.** `"desks_free"` is in `to_dict()` (`game_state.gd:1455`) and grep for
   `desks_free|hire_cap|occupied_desks` across `godot/scripts/ui` returns **zero hits**.
   The player meets the office cap only as a refusal string after clicking Send Offer.
5. **The x0.4 unproductive period** -- explained only afterwards, on the onboarding card.
6. **The 15% attrition risk** -- described as `"early-quit risk"` (`:621`), never numbered.

**And one trap worth its own line:** the mentoring prompt (`build_mentoring_prompt`,
`:610-639`) treats **lapsing or dismissing the card as choosing to skip**
(`:664-667`) -- silently arming the permanent x0.85 debuff and the 15% monthly quit roll.
A player who closes a popup has made a permanent decision and was not told so. That is a
`#1221` case: the card must say what dismissal means.

## Related

- `#789` -- hiring stitch: onboarding sub-actions as plannable sinks **at offer time**. Part
  5 is the gap report against it.
- `#1086` -- the onboard-now window tooltip omits the Attention cost and prints a raw
  `money: 3000.0`. Same $3,000 as part 5, one screen later.
- `#1091` -- every hiring route must surface the onboarding choice; no onboarded-by-silence.
  **The lapse-equals-skip trap at the end of part 5 is a live instance.**
- `#961` -- candidate pool cap; the at-cap half of part 3, already ruled.
- `#1092` -- asset sweep then bulk-generate. The closest existing container for part 1's
  persona run.
- `#793` -- office floor renders all staff as the same character. The sprite-side twin of
  part 1, and the reason to index both pools from one identity.
- `#1218` item A -- the same five hiring actions labelled "No costs" while spending 1-3
  Attention. Different defect, same five buttons.
- `#830` -- *ux(hiring): statefulness -- ask WHO, per-candidate interviews, interview popup
  w/ card+info fade-in, portraits, embedded employee panel.* The nearest existing home; part
  1 and part 2 are the measured version of its "statefulness" and "portraits" bullets.
- `#813` -- stateful candidate representation, knowledge-gated portrait to lanyard.
- `#954` -- click small pool card -> full candidate card. The natural surface for parts 1
  and 5.
- `docs/game-design/BUILD_BRIEF_HIRING_PIPELINE.md` -- already specifies most of this,
  including *"a prestige-hungry candidate takes less cash for a first-authorship promise"*
  and *"Onboard: predictable checklist (laptop, mentoring...)"*. This issue is largely a
  report that Phase B shipped its sim and not its readouts.
- `#1166` -- the promote-art route part 1 needs.

issues.title: Documentation Sync has failed on 100% of PR runs since 2026-07-28, and that taught us to ignore red
issues.body:
## The check has never passed on a PR, so nobody reads it any more

`Documentation Sync` fails on **100% of pull-request runs** and succeeds on
**100% of main runs**. Measured over the last 200 workflow runs plus the
workflow's own history:

```
3/3  fail (PR:3  main:0)   Documentation Sync
```

and, querying that workflow directly, the same split goes back to at least
**2026-07-28**:

```
failure  2026-08-22  fix/retention-counter-offers
failure  2026-08-22  fix/retention-counter-offers
failure  2026-08-22  feat/compute-engineers-are-staff
success  2026-08-12  main
failure  2026-08-12  feat/capacity-derivation
success  2026-08-05  main
failure  2026-08-05  tools/generate-tools-index
failure  2026-08-04  tools/generate-tools-index
success  2026-07-28  main
failure  2026-07-28  fix/970-noop-upgrades
success  2026-07-28  main
failure  2026-07-28  feat/hour-typing-4way
```

That is roughly four weeks of a red X that means nothing.

## Proximate cause

`.github/workflows/docs-sync.yml` has **no `permissions:` block**, so the job
runs with the repo's default read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The last step calls
`github.rest.issues.createComment(...)` (line ~120) and gets:

```
##[error]Unhandled error: HttpError: Resource not accessible by integration
  status: 403
  url: https://api.github.com/repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/issues/1271/comments
```

On `main` there is no PR to comment on, the step is skipped, and the workflow
goes green. That is why the failure is invisible in the only place anyone
looks at workflow health.

## Why this is not just a three-line fix

The literal repair is three lines:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
```

Do NOT merge that as a drive-by. Three separate questions sit on top of it,
and answering them is the actual work:

**1. Should the comment exist at all?** The comment it is trying to post says
"Download the artifact from this workflow run to preview the website export."
That is a low-value notification on every PR touching `game_state.gd`,
`actions.gd` or `events.gd` -- three of the busiest files in the repo.
Granting write permission to make a noise-comment work may be the wrong fix;
deleting the step and letting the artifact speak for itself may be the right
one. Pick deliberately.

**2. The comment body contains an emoji.** Line ~104:

```js
const comment = `## [BOOK-EMOJI] Documentation Preview
```

Issue #744 is a hard rule -- "Emoji are NEVER allowed anywhere". The blocking
gate `scripts/check_no_emoji.py` covers `godot/**/*.gd`,
`godot/data/**/*.json` and `godot/**/*.tscn`. It does **not** cover
`.github/workflows/*.yml`. So the moment this workflow is repaired it starts
posting emoji into PR comments, which is the no-emoji rule being defeated by
a surface the gate was never pointed at. Either extend the gate's file set or
decide workflows are out of scope, in writing.

**3. The generalisable defect, which is the reason to spend real time here.**
Pip's framing, 2026-08-22: *"always-fail things get ignored"*. A check that
is red 100% of the time carries zero information, and worse, it trains
everyone to read red as noise -- so the next check that goes legitimately red
is also ignored. Nothing in this repo detects that condition. Every gate we
have fires on a COMMIT; none of them watches whether a gate is *permanently*
failing.

The measurement above is cheap and mechanical, which suggests a guard in the
same anti-rot shape as the generated-index checks:

    tools/check_chronic_red.py

    Flag any workflow whose PR-branch failure rate exceeds a threshold over
    the last N runs. Report, do not block (a repo can legitimately carry a
    known-red experimental job -- but it must be DECLARED, the same way
    `Ladder-Impact: none` declares a deliberate non-bump).

Scope note: the same 200-run scan found **exactly one** chronically-red
workflow. Everything else is healthy (`Enhanced CI/CD Pipeline` 0/48,
`Quality Checks` 0/47, `Live site release freshness` 0/25, `Godot Tests`
2/30 -- real transient failures, which is what a working check looks like).
So the audit surface is small. That is a finding, not an assumption: the
guard is worth building precisely because it is cheap and there is currently
nothing between "one chronically-red workflow" and "five" except somebody
happening to notice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decided and recorded: repair the comment step, or delete it.
- [ ] `Documentation Sync` passes on a PR branch, or no longer runs on PRs.
- [ ] The emoji question is settled in writing -- either
      `scripts/check_no_emoji.py` covers `.github/workflows/**`, or a note
      says why workflows are exempt.
- [ ] A chronic-red detector exists and is run by something, with its
      threshold and window written down.
- [ ] Re-run the 200-run scan and record the resulting table in this issue,
      so the next person has a baseline rather than a hunch.

## Declaration

COMMITMENT: 2026-09-04 -- Fix the chronically-red Documentation Sync workflow and add a chronic-red detector -- owner: pdoom1-seat -- kind: task -- covers: .github/workflows/docs-sync.yml, scripts/check_no_emoji.py -- note: red on 100% of PR runs since at least 2026-07-28 and therefore invisible. Dated deliberately AFTER the travel/light-duties week and BEFORE the 2026-09-09 Manifund deadline, because the three-line permission fix is trivial but the decision it sits on (repair vs delete) and the detector are not.

RULING: 2026-08-22 -- a check that fails 100% of the time is not a check; chronic red trains the team to ignore red, so a permanently-failing gate must be either fixed or explicitly declared, never left standing -- flavour: ci-gates -- mechanism: tools/check_chronic_red.py, owed by this issue

Found while merging nine PRs on 2026-08-22; the red X on #1271 and #1277 was
this, not the PRs.

issues.title: Balance key guard covers 2 files of ~213 call sites; one live silent-fallback found in upgrades.gd
issues.body:
`test_balance_key_coverage.gd` already guards this defect class -- for TWO files. Everything else in `godot/**/*.gd` can read a Balance key that does not exist and silently use its code-side fallback. One live instance found.

## The defect class

`Balance.num("some.key", fallback)` returns the fallback when the key is absent. So a call site reading a key that does not exist LOOKS correct, behaves plausibly, and diverges from the sim the moment anyone tunes the real key. Nothing fails.

Issue **#971** already established this and built the guard: `godot/tests/unit/test_balance_key_coverage.gd`, whose docstring names the damage -- *"exactly how publish_paper/safety_research/audit_safety shipped as no-ops post-ADR-0015"*.

**But `BALANCE_KEY_SOURCES` is a list of two:**

    ACTIONS_SRC_PATH                    ("res://scripts/core/actions.gd")
    "res://autoload/event_service.gd"

Every other `.gd` file is unguarded.

## Measured, 2026-08-22

    Balance keys declared in defaults.json : 295
    Balance.* call sites in godot/**/*.gd  : 213
    DISTINCT keys read but NOT declared    : 9

Eight of the nine are FALSE POSITIVES and a widened guard must not trip on them -- they are string-prefix concatenations and format templates, not literal keys:

    doom.streams.                       doom_system.gd      (prefix + stream name)
    doom.streams.action_*               the guard test itself
    financing.                          finance_engine.gd   (prefix)
    financing.counterparty_factors.     finance_engine.gd   (prefix)
    financing.org_factors.              finance_engine.gd   (prefix)
    ledger.promise.%s.fuse_turns        ledger.gd           (format template)
    ledger.promise.%s.interest_rate     ledger.gd           (format template)
    ledger.promise.%s.principal         ledger.gd           (format template)

**The ninth is real:**

    godot/scripts/core/upgrades.gd:143
        state.global_alarm += Balance.num("doom.streams.upgrade_cat_alarm", 5.0)

`upgrade_cat_alarm` appears nowhere in `defaults.json` under any shape. It is silently using the in-code `5.0`, which is the #971 failure sitting outside the two guarded files. Whether 5.0 is the intended value is a separate question -- the point is that nothing would tell you if it were not.

## How this surfaced

Writing the #1225 item 5 fix (PR #1275) I invented `hiring.mentoring.skip_output_multiplier` and `hiring.mentoring.skip_attrition_chance` for a player-facing card. Neither exists. The card would have LOOKED right and shown stale numbers the moment the real keys (`hiring.onboarding.skimped_multiplier`, `hiring.onboarding.attrition_risk`) were tuned -- reintroducing, in the fix, the exact defect class that issue is about.

I caught it by checking. Nothing would have caught it otherwise, because `hiring_pipeline.gd` is not in the guarded list.

## Suggested scope

1. **Widen `BALANCE_KEY_SOURCES` to all of `godot/**/*.gd`** (excluding `.godot/` and, if it stays noisy, `tests/`).
2. **Skip non-literal keys rather than failing on them.** A key containing `%` or ending in `.` is a template or prefix and cannot be checked statically. Skip it and SAY SO in the output -- a silent skip is how a guard becomes decorative.
3. **Decide `doom.streams.upgrade_cat_alarm`**: declare it in `defaults.json` at its intended value, or delete the key and inline the constant. Not a judgement call this issue should make.
4. Consider whether the same scan belongs in a `tools/` script for pre-commit, or stays a GUT test. It is currently a test, which is fine and already runs in the fast gate.

## Not in scope

The trailing-prefix and `%s`-template call sites are legitimate patterns, not defects. A guard that forces them to change shape would be worse than the problem.

Filed at Pip's direction, 2026-08-22: *"we need to do an audit and a guard against that defect class... maybe as a agent / driveby / techdebt rather than getting distracted now"*.

issues.title: The Action Queue and the Attention header contradict each other in one frame -- three widgets, three data sources, one column (and 'ticks' is a word we never defined)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
**This answers the open design call in `#828` and supersedes it.** That issue asked, in
July, whether hiring actions being absent from the action queue was intended or an
inconsistency, and left it as a question. `#1041` `[2:21]` recorded the same observation
and Pip's answer ("wants both"). What is new here is that **the absence is now a visible
contradiction rather than an omission**, plus the traced mechanism, a second cause the
hiring fix would not touch, and the vocabulary problem underneath. `#828` should be closed
against this.

---

**One frame of the 2026-08-14 playtest contains a screen arguing with itself.** The
Action Queue says it is empty. The header, six inches above it, says eight Attention are
queued. The panel directly *below* the empty-state hint lists four jobs in flight. All
three are correct about the number they hold; none of them is reading the same number.

Screenshot `2026-08-14 15-12-12`, verbatim from the pixels:

| Surface | What it said | What it was reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top bar | `Attention: 20 (12 free, 8 queued)` | `month_plan.attention_spent` (`main_ui.gd:1176-1195`) |
| Attention gauge | `ATTENTION ********ooooooooooo  - 8/20 allocated - 0 reserved` | the same scalar (`plan_screen.gd:89-107`) |
| **Action Queue** | **`No actions queued yet -- click an action to add it here.`** | **`PlanController.queued_actions`, a UI-only mirror (`plan_controller.gd:30`)** |
| IN-FLIGHT HIRING | `Offer: Iris Wilson 0/2 ticks` (x3 + `Networking: sourcing a lead`) | `HiringPipeline.jobs` (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:570-666`) |

Three data sources, one column of the screen, no arbitration.

## Why they disagree -- the exact mechanism

`month_plan.attention_spent` has **two disjoint sets of writers, and only one of them
mints a queue tile.**

**Writer A -- mints a tile.** `GameManager.select_action()`,
`godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:274-278`: debits `attention_spent`, then appends to
`state.queued_actions`; the view mirrors it via `submenu_controller.gd:158-160` ->
`plan_controller.queue_action()`, and a tile appears.

**Writer B -- mints nothing.** `MonthPlan.spend_attention()`,
`godot/scripts/core/month_plan.gd:252-268`. Its own docstring states the intent plainly:

> Spend `cost` Attention from the AVAILABLE (un-reserved) pool at plan speed, **without
> minting a queued-strategic WIP entry**. This is the primitive the hiring pipeline (and
> other duration subsystems that track their own jobs) use: the founder currency is still
> debited here, but the duration/target bookkeeping lives in the subsystem.

Every hiring action is Writer B:

| Action | Attention | Debit site | Job recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `advertise` | 3 | `hiring_pipeline.gd:114-117` | `campaigns` (`:121-125`) -- **rendered nowhere at all** |
| `use_connections` | 2 | `:138-141` | `jobs` (`:143-150`) |
| `interview_next` | 2 | `:208-209` | `jobs` (`:211-217`) |
| `hire_best` (offer) | 1 | `:287-288` | `jobs` (`:294-300`) |
| `onboard_next` | 1-2 per hire | `:473-501`, `:533` | onboarding flags |

The hiring panel's result handler (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:398-406`) refreshes the
header and the in-flight panel and **never calls `update_queued_actions_display()`**. So
the design intent -- "the subsystem tracks its own jobs" -- is honoured in the sim and
abandoned in the UI: the founder currency moves on the shared readout while the shared
readout's neighbour insists nothing is happening.

**The screenshot's own arithmetic:** three offers (1 each) + one connections (2) = 5. The
missing 3 is almost certainly one `advertise`, which appends to `campaigns` -- a list
**neither** widget reads. So part of that 8 is invisible in *both* panels, not just the
queue.

**A second, independent cause of the same contradiction.** At commit,
`main_ui.gd:1042` and `:1070` call `plan_controller.reset_mirror()`
(`plan_controller.gd:100-106`), which empties the mirror with no refund, while
`attention_spent` persists until `MonthPlan.begin_month()` (`month_plan.gd:127-129`).
**After any commit the widget is empty by construction while the header still reports the
month's spend as "queued".** Fixing only the hiring seam leaves this one standing.

(Third, latent: `MonthPlan.queued_strategic` is rendered only by `QueueGantt`
(`queue_gantt.gd:36-49`), which is gated to the `proposed` layout at `main_ui.gd:776`.
`#1221` establishes that lane has no production writer, so it is always empty too.)

## The second half: "ticks" is not a word we have ever defined

Pip flagged `0/2 ticks` as jargon. It is worth being precise about what kind of problem
that is, because it is **not** a hidden-cost problem of the `#1218` family.

**The durations are real, declared, Balance-driven, and correct:**

| Kind | Balance key | Value | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| connections | `hiring.connections.duration_ticks` | 2 | `godot/data/balance/defaults.json:57` |
| interview | `hiring.interview.duration_ticks` | 3 | `defaults.json:58` |
| offer | `hiring.offer.duration_ticks` | 2 | `defaults.json:59` |

The UI reads the same keys with the same fallbacks (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:604-610`),
so the bars cannot drift from the sim. **Nothing is hidden. It is illegible.**

A tick is a turn is one workday -- `clock.gd:5` (`One turn = one WORKDAY`), `clock.gd:13`
(`TURNS_PER_WEEK = 5`), `clock.gd:29-32`; jobs resolve on
`state.turn + duration_ticks` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:149, 215, 298`) inside
`HiringPipeline.on_tick()` (`:692-705`), one per `MonthController.advance_tick()`.

**The word is defined nowhere a player can reach.** `grep -i tick docs/PLAYERGUIDE.md` ->
zero hits. `docs/GLOSSARY.md`'s only "tick" is a release-version example (`:110`). The
only in-game tooltip that explains it (`queue_gantt.gd:142`, *"Lands on resolution tick
(turn) %d."*) is in the proposed layout the player is not running.

**And the game already renders the identical quantity as "days" elsewhere:**

| String | Where | Word |
|---|---|---|
| `%d/%d ticks` | `hiring_panel_controller.gd:662` + `:616` | **ticks** |
| `%d/%d steps` | same line, `:637` -- onboarding | **steps** (fair: checklist items, not time) |
| `~$%d bills in %d ticks` | `finance_engine.gd:340` | **ticks** |
| `Back from %s after %d days.` (value is `ticks_resolved`) | `conference_trip.gd:383` | **days** |
| `%d days away \| %d Attention consumed` (also `ticks_resolved`) | `conference_vignette.gd:155,164` | **days** |
| `day %d -- %s %d` | `screen_mode.gd:174` | **day** |

The travel surfaces already made the right call. Hiring did not. And because `3/4 steps`
and `0/2 ticks` sit in the same list under one `IN-FLIGHT HIRING` header, they read as the
same kind of progress when one is a clock and the other is a checklist.

## What a fix has to decide

1. **One list, or one honest label.** Either the queue widget renders in-flight hiring
   (and advertising campaigns) as tiles, or the header stops calling `attention_spent`
   "queued". The current pairing is the only combination that is wrong on its face.
2. **The post-commit case** (`reset_mirror` vs. persistent `attention_spent`) must be
   handled or the contradiction survives the fix.
3. **`advertise` leaves no trace anywhere.** `campaigns` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:121`) has no
   renderer. A player who spends 3 Attention and $8,000 on it can see the money leave and
   has no surface that says a campaign is running. See the hiring issue for the rest of
   that story.
4. **Say "days".** One word, three call sites, and it is the word the rest of the game
   already uses.

## Related

- `#828` -- *hiring actions don't appear in the action queue*. **Superseded by this.** Its
  design question ("where should hiring commitments surface?") is answered by the fact that
  the header already claims they are in the queue.
- `#1041` `[2:21]` -- *"Hiring actions stack in the in-flight section but do not create
  cards in the action queue. Pip wants both."* Same observation, three weeks earlier, from
  the same person.
- `#1044` -- *actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no rhythm*. Its item 3 --
  *"the queue should promise a completion time... once actions take time, the queue stops
  being a list and becomes a schedule"* -- is the destination this widget is heading for.
  **Hiring is currently the only thing in the game that does take time**, which is why it is
  the first system to break the widget. Read before designing the fix.
- `#794` -- *PLAN operations gantt: bigger font/area + a 'what's next / ETA to land'
  indicator*. The ETA half of that ask is this widget. Whoever picks this up should read
  it first; the two should not be built twice.
- `#1037` / `#1208` / `#1209` -- the vocabulary lane. The "ticks" half of this issue is the
  same shape as those three: a term of art printed on screen and defined nowhere. `#1037`
  also records that `GLOSSARY.md` has no player-facing counterpart, which is where "day"
  would be defined once.
- `#1218` -- the hidden-Attention audit. **This is deliberately not that:** these costs are
  disclosed. The complaint is arithmetic that does not add up on screen.
- `#1219` -- silent submenu rejections, same hiring path, different failure (nothing
  queued *and* nothing said). Fixing that one makes this one more visible, not less.

issues.title: score_api.php truncates the leaderboard before checking json_encode succeeded -- one submitted name empties it
issues.body:
**Routed from the 2026-08-22 coordination burndown. This is a data-destruction path in a live public API, and the fix is one conditional.**

`server/leaderboard/score_api.php:139` calls `ftruncate($fp, 0)` **unconditionally on the result of `json_encode()`**, with no `=== false` check.

`json_encode()` returns `false` on failure — malformed UTF-8 in a submitted field is the ordinary way that happens, and this endpoint accepts player-supplied names. So the sequence is:

1. A name arrives that `json_encode()` cannot encode.
2. `json_encode()` returns `false`.
3. The file is truncated to zero anyway.
4. `false` is written, which is the empty string.

**One submitted name empties the leaderboard.** No exploit required, no authentication bypass, no cleverness — a player with the wrong characters in their handle does it by accident.

## The fix

Check the encode before truncating. Truncate only once you have bytes to write:

```php
$json = json_encode($data);
if ($json === false) {
    // do NOT truncate. The existing file is better than an empty one.
    return error(500, 'encode failed: ' . json_last_error_msg());
}
ftruncate($fp, 0);
fwrite($fp, $json);
```

## Second, smaller

`ALLOWED_FIELDS` (line 30) does not include `operator_name`. Confirmed 2026-08-22 against the current repo state.

## What is NOT known from here

**The deployed copy's state is UNKNOWN.** This repo contains no deploy path for `score_api.php`, and verifying what is actually running needs SSH to the host. **Do not assume the live file matches the repo** — check it, and say which you checked. That distinction is the difference between fixing this and believing you have.

## Why it survived

This sits behind the same class the estate has been finding all week: the failure produces no error at the moment it happens. A truncated leaderboard reads as "nobody is playing", which is indistinguishable from a quiet day, and `ok:true` comes back either way.

issues.title: RELEASING.md says ship from a release branch; four releases shipped from main and CI has no release/* handling
issues.body:
`RELEASING.md` says "ship from the release branch, never from churny `main`". Four releases have shipped from `main`, and the CI workflow has no `release/*` handling at all.

## The protocol

`RELEASING.md` -- **ACTIVE PROTOCOL, ratified 2026-07-25 (#775)**:

> **Each monthly epoch, cut a release branch.** At the epoch (1st Friday), cut `release/v0.X` from the epoch commit and tag `v0.X.0`. That branch is the stable line for the whole month.
>
> **Ship from the release branch, never from churny `main`.** Builds and tags come off `release/v0.X`; `main` keeps absorbing the next epoch's work.

## What is actually true

    git ls-remote --heads origin 'release/*'   -> (nothing)

v0.13.0, v0.13.1, v0.13.2, v0.14.0, v0.14.1 and v0.14.2 were all tagged off `main`. **The release-branch half of this protocol has never been exercised.**

`#775`'s own acceptance list had three items:

| Criterion | State |
|---|---|
| hotpatch criteria list written | DONE -- `RELEASING.md`, four numbered criteria |
| RELEASING.md documents the flow | DONE -- 64 lines, clear |
| **CI release workflow understands `release/*` branches** | **NOT DONE** |

`.github/workflows/enhanced-release.yml` triggers on `push: tags: 'v*.*.*'` plus `workflow_dispatch`. There is no `release/*` branch trigger, no branch-aware build path, and nothing that distinguishes a tag cut from a release branch from a tag cut from `main`.

#775 was closed COMPLETED on 2026-07-25 with **no comments**, so nothing recorded that the third criterion was outstanding.

## Why this is worth doing before September

`docs/ROADMAP.md` puts **v0.15 on Sep 4** -- the next monthly epoch, and the first cut where the protocol says a `release/v0.15` branch must exist. Discovering on epoch night that the release workflow does not recognise the branch is a bad evening, and epoch nights already carry the [Gate 4]/[Gate 5]/[Gate 6] ceremony and a hard 17:30 stop.

The failure mode is not subtle but it IS late-breaking: the tag fires the workflow, the workflow builds whatever it is pointed at, and nobody finds out the branch was irrelevant until someone asks which commit shipped.

## Suggested scope

1. Teach `enhanced-release.yml` about `release/*` -- at minimum, verify that a tag being built is reachable from the expected release branch, and say so in the build summary.
2. **Rehearse it once before Sep 4.** Cut a throwaway `release/v0.14-rehearsal` from the v0.14.2 tag, push a `v0.14.2-rc` style tag, watch the workflow, delete both. A protocol that has never been run is a hypothesis.
3. Record the outcome in `RELEASING.md`'s worked-example section, which currently documents v0.13 -- a release that predates the protocol.

## Not in scope

The trunk model itself is settled and correct: `main` is trunk, `main` IS the stash, no `develop` (ADR-0001). Nothing here reopens that. This is only about the release-branch half never having been wired up or run.

Found while checking whether a long-lived feature branch was permitted for #1247. It is not -- the protocol is explicit -- and reading it surfaced this.

issues.title: P6 needs a mechanism or deletion: the worktree rule was broken by an agent on 2026-08-21
issues.body:
**Drafted 2026-08-21 by the pdoom1-website seat. Mechanism designed and MEASURED in a throwaway repo, not built here. This is a ruling request, and it carries its own deletion trigger.**

Raised because P6's falsifier fired on 2026-08-21: an agent performed six checkouts and a `git reset --hard` in the shared main checkout while another seat was working there. See `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-08-07_CAPTURE.md` section 6a.

# P6: give the rule a mechanism, or delete it

For Pip. Measured today on git 2.52.0.windows.1 / Git Bash, not recalled; no
repo file modified.

## 1. The decision

P6 reads "No agent operates in the main checkout; lanes get worktrees." Its
falsifier fired: `git reflog` in `D:/Local_Code/pdoom1` shows six
`checkout: moving from X to Y` plus one `reset: moving to origin/main` between
05:20 and 05:59 UTC today, while another seat held work in that tree. Nothing
was lost only because that work sat on a branch. It built an isolated worktree four hours
later once it noticed staged work, so the rule is operable, just not operated. A rule broken and kept reads as a control
in every future audit. Choose: **(a)** wire the mechanism below, or **(b)**
delete P6.

## 2. Detection — read this before the candidates

**Retrospective attribution is impossible here, which kills any audit-shaped
mechanism outright.** Measured:

| Source | Agent vs Pip | Discriminates? |
|---|---|---|
| reflog ident `%gn/%ge`, author `%an/%ae`, message `%gs` | byte-identical | **No** |
| `$CLAUDECODE`, `$AI_AGENT` | `1` / `claude-code_2-1-233_agent` vs unset | **Yes, live only** |

The reflog stores no environment. So P6's own falsifier — "read `git reflog`...
any agent-attributable reset" — **is not machine-checkable as written**; today's attribution came
from session context, not git. A mechanism must therefore fire *at
the moment of the operation*, inside the process running git. Both vars reach
hook processes (verified); neither survives into history.

## 3. Candidates

**M1 — `reference-transaction` hook, blocking.** *Detects:* any ref write by a process
carrying `$CLAUDECODE`/`$AI_AGENT`, main checkout only (`git rev-parse
--git-dir` equals `--git-common-dir` only there). *Lives:* `.git/hooks/reference-transaction`,
hand-installed — the pre-commit framework does **not** support this hook type,
the one place "extend what exists" fails. *Measured:* agent
`checkout` and agent `reset --hard` both exit 128 with HEAD unmoved; agent
commit inside a linked worktree exits 0; **human** checkout exits 0.
*Cost:* the naive form also blocks `git worktree add` — the remedy it demands —
and `fetch`; the tuned form allows `refs/remotes/*`, `ORIG_HEAD`, `AUTO_MERGE`,
`refs/stash` and a `PDOOM1_MAIN_CHECKOUT_OK=1` hatch (retested, all four cases
correct). Per-checkout, inert until installed. *Forced failure:* feed it a `HEAD` line on stdin with `CLAUDECODE=1`, assert
exit 1; repeat under `env -u CLAUDECODE -u AI_AGENT`, assert exit 0.

**M2 — `post-checkout` tripwire, detection only.** *Detects:* an agent-attributed branch
switch, logged to a ledger `quality-checks.yml` asserts is empty. *Lives:* a
`stages: [post-checkout]` entry beside `class-cache-check`, which already
installs that stage — genuinely extends what exists. *Cost:* **measured — `post-checkout` never fires on `git reset --hard`.**
Today's incident contained one hard reset, so M2 is blind to the most dangerous
of the seven operations, and fires after the damage. *Forced failure:*
invoke with synthetic SHAs and `CLAUDECODE=1`, assert non-zero.

**M3 — delete P6**, replaced by: "agents must not `reset` a tree they did not
create."

## 4. Weakest, and whether deletion wins

**M2 is weakest; do not build it** — it cannot see resets, the whole of today's
risk. **Deletion is not right:** the rule is not aspirational, and M1 was built
and made to both block and permit in about ten minutes. But delete P6 if M1 is
not installed this week — an uninstalled hook plus a written rule is worse than
no rule, because it adds the appearance of enforcement.

**Honest limit: M1 is a tripwire, not a cage.** An agent that hits the refusal
can export `PDOOM1_MAIN_CHECKOUT_OK=1`; one that edits files can delete the
hook. It turns a silent slip into a loud deliberate act — and today's incident *was*
an unnoticed slip, so it is aimed at the observed failure mode, not an
adversary. Say so in the rule's text, or the next audit over-credits it.

**MAX_PATH:** the remedy must name a short root. `D:/pd1wt/<lane>` worked today;
one under the temp path failed with "Filename too long".

## 5. Today

Install M1 tuned, plus its two-direction test. `pre-commit install` does not
cover this hook, so the per-checkout setup step must name it. Rewrite P6 as
what it becomes: *"An agent writing refs
in the main pdoom1 checkout is refused by `.git/hooks/reference-transaction`.
The refusal is bypassable, deliberately. Lanes get worktrees under
`D:/pd1wt/`."* Re-falsify by asserting the hook is installed and its test passes — not by
reading the reflog, which cannot answer.
